workloads.interpretation: Qwen3.5-9B scores 82.5 on MMLU-Pro and 65.6 on LiveCodeBench. The 120B gpt-oss checkpoint scores 80.8 and 82.7 respectively. Select the coding, instruction or long-document test that matches your workload.

workloads.name: Embeddings
workloads.description: Mean task score across multilingual embedding tasks.

comparisons.description: Finding relevant documents for a query in the multilingual MTEB retrieval tasks.
Finding translations of sentences across languages.
Agreement with human ratings of sentence-pair similarity.

workloads.interpretation: For multilingual search, compare retrieval directly. BGE-M3 scores 79.11 on bitext mining and 54.60 on retrieval. A model that pairs translations well can still miss relevant passages.

workloads.name: Image generation
workloads.description: Object composition in 1024px images, including counts, colors and positions.

comparisons.description: Following dense prompts with multiple objects, attributes and relationships.
Distance between generated and reference image distributions under the publisher’s 1024px protocol.
Alignment between the image and its text prompt under the publisher’s 1024px protocol.

workloads.interpretation: At 1024px, SANA 1.5 1.6B and 4.8B score 0.82 and 0.81 on GenEval. Their DPG scores reverse the order, 84.5 and 84.7. These small gaps make the target prompt and available memory relevant to the choice.

workloads.name: Transcription
workloads.description: English word error rate on clean audiobook speech.

comparisons.description: English word error rate on the harder audiobook split.
English word error rate on meeting recordings with the leaderboard’s cleaned references.
English word error rate on the cleaned, audio-aligned and chunked earnings-call split.

workloads.interpretation: The best clean-audiobook result here is Parakeet v2 at 1.28% word error. For earnings calls, v3 leads at 5.85%. Meeting audio produces more errors across this group, so use that column for a meeting transcription shortlist.

workloads.name: Vision & language
workloads.description: Accuracy on multimodal questions across academic subjects.

comparisons.description: Average edit distance on document parsing. Smaller values mean the extracted content is closer to the reference.
Accuracy on mathematical reasoning problems that require visual input.

workloads.interpretation: For scanned pages, switch to OmniDocBench. Gemma 4 E4B reduces average edit distance to 0.181 from E2B’s 0.290. For figures in math problems, inspect MATH-Vision instead.

workloads.name: Speech synthesis
workloads.description: Transcript error on synthesized Mandarin speech in the Seed-TTS test set.

comparisons.description: Transcript error on synthesized English speech in the Seed-TTS test set.

workloads.interpretation: The Seed-TTS scores measure whether the intended words survive synthesis. Choose the language you need, then audition samples for pronunciation, pacing and resemblance to the voice you want.

workloads.name: Music generation
workloads.description: Distance between generated and reference audio distributions on the released instrumental models.

comparisons.description: Alignment of generated instrumental music with the MusicCaps text description.
SongBench average over seven automatic quality dimensions. The WildSongBench evaluation uses 192 prompts and selects the lower-error of two candidates for these systems.
Phoneme error rate for sung lyrics. The WildSongBench evaluation uses 192 prompts and selects the lower-error of two candidates for these systems.

workloads.interpretation: Use MusicCaps for instrumental prompts and WildSongBench for full songs. YuE2 leads this group on the SongBench average, while MiniMax Music 3 has the lowest sung-phoneme error. Listen for phrasing and intelligibility on your own lyrics.

workloads.name: Video generation
workloads.description: Overall video benchmark score in the 720p comparison.

comparisons.description: Visual quality in the ContentV comparison, aggregated across VBench quality dimensions.
Aggregate semantic score in the ContentV comparison, measuring how closely generated content follows the requested concepts.
Amount of motion in the ContentV comparison. Larger scores indicate more dynamic output.

workloads.interpretation: Start with the 720p total for the three checkpoints tested together. The ContentV comparison breaks out motion and prompt semantics across a wider set. A high dynamic-degree score favors movement, which can be undesirable in a locked-off shot.

workloads.name: Reranking
workloads.description: English MTEB v2 retrieval subset. Rerankers score candidate passages against a query.

comparisons.description: Reranking on the Chinese MTEB v1 retrieval subset.
Multilingual long-document retrieval.
Ranking code passages for retrieval queries.

workloads.interpretation: Reranking is a second pass over retrieved candidates. Qwen3-Reranker-4B edges out 8B on English MTEB-R, while 8B leads on the Chinese subset. Compare the metric for the language or code corpus you actually index.
